title: Microsoft Research releases Magnetar zero-knowledge virtual machine
excerpt: The system proves program execution for RISC-V architectures using standard hash functions for security.
bodyHtml:
Microsoft Research announced Magnetar on October 15, 2026, a zero-knowledge virtual machine, or zkVM. The system allows developers to write programs in Rust, Go, or C and receive a cryptographic certificate that the program ran correctly. Magnetar proves the execution of RISC-V, an open processor architecture with mature compilers for every mainstream language.

According to Microsoft Research, Magnetar proves 7.2 to 8.7 million processor instructions per second on a laptop. Across 15 benchmark programs, the system is 10 to 39 times faster on average than the fastest existing zkVMs on the same machine. An optimized version of Magnetar proves 9.5–12.8 million cycles per second, and its proofs verify in about 12 milliseconds.

The system relies on standard hash functions such as SHA-256 or SHA-3. It requires no elliptic curves, no lattices, no special-purpose hash functions, no trusted setup, and no unproven conjecture about error-correcting codes.
